text:
Marta R.: hey team, quick heads-up — i'm pulling primary for the next 4h due to a family emergency. Samir will be secondary but he's on call from a different timezone and might have a 20-30m delay for wakeup pages. i'm posting the short plan here so the bridge/alerts are clear :wave:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-045 - intermittent serving latency affecting eu-west. Triggered by 95th pct > 800ms for 3 consecutive minutes. :rotating_light:
Samir Patel: thanks, marta. can you confirm which routes are impacted? i'll keep my phone on loud but want to make sure we minimize false wakeups.
Marta R.: looks like inference-gateway-eu and batch-ingest-eu. dashboard: https://redwood.example.com/inc/INC-2026-045. customer impact: a subset of active sessions seeing generation timeouts and client retries. not full outage but noticeable for a few customers.
Chris L.: tagging escalation rules — per runbook we page Kevin (SRE Lead) immediately for widespread latency >15% user impact or 95th>1s. Since this is 95th=800ms and partial customer retries, we should first attempt mitigation on-call (primary + secondary) and only escalate if mitigation fails in 20 minutes. agree? :thinking_face:
Alice G.: agree with Chris. quick checklist: 1) verify the affected pods (k8s: eu-*), 2) check model variant rollbacks, 3) look for autoscaler thrash, 4) increase short-term concurrency limit to reduce queueing.
Samir Patel: can we get a short list of who to page if we escalate? i'll put names in my phone.
Marta R.: page order for this class of incident (latency, partial customer impact): first oncall-sre (me), then secondary (Samir), then SRE Lead (Kevin), then Infra Lead (tag on Slack), then Eng Runtime pager if kernel-level or GPU hotplug suspected. for quick copy paste: ``page Kevin -> page Infra -> page Eng Runtime``
Chris L.: adding nuance: if you see 5xxs or error rate spike alongside latency, escalate immediately. paging rule in runbook: ``if error_rate_delta > 2% OR customer-visible retries > 10% within 10m => immediate escalate to SRE Lead``
oncall-bot: autocreated bridge: https://meet.redwood.example.com/bridges/INC-2026-045. Bridge mode: adhoc. Participants: Marta R., Samir Patel.
Kevin (SRE Lead): thanks for the ping. i'm on standby. if you need me upstream i can join in 10. can someone capture the first 10 slow traces and paste? that helps root cause quickly.
Alice G.: grabbing traces now. here's one slow tail from the logs:
```
TRACE_ID: a1b2c3
route: inference-gateway-eu/predict
latency_ms: 1280
node: eu-node-17
error: none
cpu: 72% gpu_mem: 58%
queue_len: 27
```
Samir Patel: queue_len 27 on eu-node-17 is likely the hot spot. i can try temporary traffic-shed to reduce queueing or increase replicas. which is preferable?
Marta R.: prefer scale-up first (fast path): increase replicas for inference-gateway-eu by +2 and bump replica for model-worker-eu by +1. also toggle KV cache warming off/on? (alice?)
Alice G.: KV cache warming toggles are risky mid-incident. try replica scale first. i'll watch model-worker metrics in case of ramp-up cold-starts.
Chris L.: for scaling, use the quick command in runbook: ``kubectl -n prod scale deploy inference-gateway-eu --replicas=6`` (confirm current is 4). also run `kubectl get hpa inference-gateway-eu -o yaml` to verify no HPA conflict.
Samir Patel: doing scale now. will watch latencies.
Samir Patel: scaled. immediate drop in queue_len to ~8 on eu-node-17, 95th dropped to ~420ms. looks promising.
Marta R.: great. holding for 20m observation window. if 95th stays <500ms we do not page further. if it creeps back above 700ms or errors spike, escalate to Kevin.
Kevin (SRE Lead): sounds good. if you need me earlier, react with :phone: and i'll join. also FYI, infra-bot shows a noisy NIC on eu-node-17 from last night maintenance log — possible network hiccups.
infra-bot: maintenance note: eu-node-17 had interface flap 03:12 UTC, vendor doctoring performed; no persistent errors detected.
Alice G.: good catch. i'll add checking `ethtool -S` on that node if we see regression. for now, monitoring deck updated and alert suppressed to prevent noisy paging.
Marta R.: tiny ops: Samir, once observation window is clear, please annotate incident with `primary_swap_note` and list the temporary scaling commands used. that helps postmortem.
Samir Patel: will do. also setting my phone to high-priority for the next 2h in case things revert.
Chris L.: documenting escalation snippet here for others to copy: ``IF partial-latency AND mitigated-within-20m -> no escalation. IF reverts OR error-rate spike OR customer-visible retries persist -> PAGE Kevin (SRE Lead) -> PAGE infra on-call -> open bridging with Eng Runtime.``
Marta R.: thanks all. last check before I sign off: any objections to me leaving primary now and letting Samir act as warm backup?
Kevin (SRE Lead): no objections. team, great coordination. Samir, you're effectively primary for wakeups until Marta returns. marshal as needed.
Samir Patel: acknowledged. i'll keep the bridge open for 30m then close if stable.
Marta R.: thanks team. i'm off now. leaving notes in the incident and runbook link: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/latency-response. :heart:
Chris L.: thanks marta — take care. everyone else, please update the incident timeline with timestamps of scaling and metrics snapshots.
oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-045 updated: status=mitigated -> monitoring. log: scale action applied by Samir.
Marta R.: (final) if anything flares, page me anyway. i might be reachable. peace. :wave:
